summary: Kodo Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his master's (around 1956–1958) and earned his doctorate in 1984 at Komazawa University. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1960 to 2004.
Kodo Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1904 to 1907. He later served as a researcher at Taisho University.

Kodo Sawaki worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Koho Sawada, Zenko Sawada, Sotan Oka, Ryo-un Fueoka, and Join Saeki, and at Horyuji Kangakuin. He was a professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (c. 1949–1965).
Kodo Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University studying under Shiro Matsumoto and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.

Koen Wellens is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and completed a PhD at the University of Oslo under the doctoral supervision of Per Kværne.

Koenraad Elst works in Indology, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at KU Leuven from around 1977 to 1999, earning an MA, and also studied at Banaras Hindu University between around 1988 and 1992.

Kogen Mizuno was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo in 1928. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo and held posts as professor and president (1976) at Komazawa University.
Koichi Hiraoka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University from around 1980 to 1984 and is attested as a visiting professor at Shuchiin University in 2026.

Koichi Hokazono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD at Kyushu University. He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1995) and Kagoshima International University (attested 1991–2000).

Koichi Shinohara works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He served as professor at McMaster University (c. 1976–2004), Numata Program coordinator at the University of Toronto Mississauga (2004), and senior lecturer at Yale University (c. 2004–2017).

Koichi Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Supervised by Yasunori Ejima and Akira Saito, he earned his PhD from the University of Tokyo in 2004, later serving there as assistant, project researcher, and professor (attested 2026).

Koichi Yokoyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Akira Hirakawa and Gyōin Hashimoto, completing an MA at the University of Tokyo (c. 1965–1970). He served as assistant professor at Rikkyo University from around 1973 to 2006.
Koin Takada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gyōin Hashimoto from around 1937, succeeding him in 1967. He also studied at Ryukoku University from around 1944 to 1947.

Koji Kamioka worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under Yutaka Ochihara at Kyoto University (c. 1957–1963) and held posts as lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969) and member at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

Koji Shindo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was a graduate student at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026) and served as a part-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

Koji Takahashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (c. 1953–1957) and received a doctorate from Bukkyo University in 1991. He served as an assistant professor (c. 1967–2005) and professor (c. 1976–2005) at Bukkyo University.

Koji Tanaka is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at Macquarie University, the University of Auckland (attested 2011–2014), and the Australian National University's School of Philosophy.

Kojiro Yoshikawa was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University from around 1923 to 1926. He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (c. 1947–1967) and president of Toho Gakkai (c. 1971–1980).

Kojun Fukui was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied under Sokichi Tsuda at Waseda University (PhD 1949). He served as professor at Waseda University (1941–1969) and president of Taisho University (1928–1968, 1972–1975).
